angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 12,589,012 km at 130.97 pc = 1.29 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.6353 +/- 0.1109 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 130.97 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 18.095 (17.672 to 18.540) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 12,589,012 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 4.080 (4.040 to 4.120) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5824 +/- 3.8 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1824277055360974720: teff_gspphot 5823.648 K (16th-84th percentiles 5819.8896-5827.5435), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1824277055360974720: teff_gspphot 5823.648 K (16th-84th percentiles 5819.8896-5827.5435), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/sham.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.534, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
